lines: 你大概每天都在和它聊天：问问题、写代码、改文章。
You probably chat with it every day: asking questions, writing code, editing essays.
但你想过吗，它的内部到底在发生什么？
But have you ever wondered what is actually happening inside it?
这是「大语言模型」课程的第零章：导读。
This is Chapter 0 of the Large Language Model course: the orientation.
这一集不讲公式，只做一件事：给你一张地图。
No formulas today. Just one job: give you a map.
一张能装进脑子、也能随时翻回来的地图。
A map that fits in your head, and that you can come back to.
七十年的人工智能研究，能不能压缩成一句话？
Can seventy years of AI research be squeezed into one sentence?
可以。大语言模型，是用海量文本训练出来的程序。
Yes. A large language model is a program trained on enormous amounts of text.
它只擅长一件事：根据上文，猜下一个词。
It is good at one thing: guessing the next word from the preceding text.
你手机的输入法，其实每天都在做类似的事。
The keyboard on your phone does something similar every day.
比如这一句：今天下雨了，出门记得带……
Take this sentence: It is raining, remember to bring your...
下一个词，最可能是「伞」。
The most likely next word is umbrella.
但模型不是查表，它给每个候选词打分。
But the model does not look up a table; it scores every candidate.
挑一个接上，再把新词放回上文，继续猜。
It picks one, appends it, puts it back into the context, and guesses again.
目标很朴素，可当模型大到一定程度，奇怪的事发生了。
The goal is plain. But once the model gets big enough, something strange happens.
翻译、推理、写代码，没有人专门教过它。
Translation, reasoning, coding: nobody taught it these directly.
这些能力，是在预测下一个词的过程中长出来的。
They grew out of the single task of predicting the next word.
我们管它们叫：副产品。
We call them by-products.
不过，这句话里的每个词，都值得怀疑。
But every word in that sentence deserves suspicion.
第一，为什么猜下一个词，能逼出推理？
First: why would guessing the next word produce reasoning?
第二，「大到一定程度」到底是多大？
Second: how big is big enough?
为什么是突然变好，而不是慢慢变好？
Why does it improve suddenly, instead of gradually?
第三，猜得准，就等于理解吗？
Third: does guessing well mean understanding?
第四，如果它只是在猜，为什么会一本正经地胡说？
Fourth: if it is only guessing, why does it state nonsense so confidently?
整门课，就是把这四个问题，一层一层拆开。
This whole course takes those four questions apart, layer by layer.
拆完以后，你能读懂论文摘要，也能判断新闻有没有夸大。
Afterwards, you can read a paper abstract and judge whether a headline exaggerates.
先看地图。左边是目标，右边有五个模块。
Start with the map. The goal is on the left; five modules are on the right.
目标是预测下一个词；五个模块，是支撑它的柱子。
The goal is predicting the next word; five modules are the pillars beneath it.
表示：词怎么变成向量。
Representation: how words become vectors.
架构：Transformer 怎么组织计算。
Architecture: how a Transformer organises computation.
数据：互联网文本，怎么变成训练材料。
Data: how internet text becomes training material.
规模：为什么越大越好，还能讲出规律。
Scale: why bigger is better, and why the law is predictable.
对齐：怎么让它听人类的话。
Alignment: how to make it follow human intent.
如果只记五个词：预测、表示、架构、规模、对齐。
If you remember only five words: prediction, representation, architecture, scale, alignment.
这张地图，画了七十多年，大致分成五个时代。
This map took over seventy years to draw, and falls into five eras.
1948 到 2002：统计时代，靠数数估计下一个词的概率。
1948 to 2002: the statistical era, estimating next-word probabilities by counting.
2003 到 2016：神经时代，神经网络代替数数，词也变成向量。
2003 to 2016: the neural era, replacing counts with networks and words with vectors.
2017 到 2019：Transformer 时代，更并行，也更会看全局。
2017 to 2019: the Transformer era, more parallel, and aware of the whole context.
2020 到 2022：规模时代，越大越好，背后有数学规律。
2020 to 2022: the scale era, where the rule that bigger is better follows a law.
2022 年到现在：对齐与推理时代，从会说话，到听话，再到会想。
2022 to now: alignment and reasoning, from talking, to following, to thinking.
注意，这些年代只是大致边界；五个时代，是同一条主线的五次换挡。
Note: these dates are rough boundaries; five eras, five gear changes on one road.
把五个时代放在一起看，有一个反复出现的模式。
Put the five eras side by side and a pattern keeps returning.
每一次跃迁，都是把一个手工设计的部件，换成从数据里学出来的部件。
Every leap swaps a hand-designed part for a part learned from data.
统计模型的回退规则是人写的，神经网络把它学了出来。
Back-off rules were written by hand; neural networks learned them.
循环网络逐词传递，是架构强加的限制，注意力把它放开了。
Recurrent nets passed words one at a time; attention removed that limit.
有用、无害、诚实，本来是人写的规则，RLHF 改成从比较里学。
Helpful, harmless, honest were hand-written rules; RLHF learned them from comparisons.
然后，再靠规模，把这个新部件推向质变。
Then scale pushes the new part over a threshold.
生物学里管这叫「预适应」：羽毛最初为了保暖，后来用来飞行。
Biology calls this exaptation: feathers first for warmth, later for flight.
说完内容，再说这门课怎么写。
Now, how is this course written?
很多教程，第一章讲 softmax，第四章再讲一遍，第九章又讲一遍。
Many tutorials explain softmax in chapter one, again in four, again in nine.
这门课换了个做法：每个概念只定义一次。
This course does it differently: each concept is defined once.
第一次出现时，给定义、给直觉、给一个例子，然后登记进概念账本。
When a concept first appears, it gets a definition, an intuition, an example, and a ledger entry.
之后再见，只写「见某节」，不再解释。
Later chapters simply point back to that section.
每章开头，还会写清「新增」了什么，「前置」需要什么。
Every chapter opens with what is new and what is assumed.
同一个例子，也绝不用第二次。
And no example is ever used twice.
因为工作记忆很有限，重复会挤掉真正的新东西。
Working memory is limited; repetition crowds out what is truly new.
最后，换一个角度看这些零件。
Finally, look at these parts from another angle.
熵来自热力学，被信息论借走，最后成了训练模型的损失函数。
Entropy came from thermodynamics, was borrowed by information theory, and became the loss.
梯度下降，和细菌朝着养分游动，是同一个算法。
Gradient descent is the same algorithm as bacteria swimming toward nutrients.
混合专家模型，就是亚当·斯密别针工厂里的分工。
Mixture of experts is the division of labour in Adam Smith's pin factory.
生物学里的预适应，也是同一个模式：旧结构，新用途。
Biology's exaptation is the same pattern: an old structure, a new use.
类比是迁移知识的好工具，但也可能是陷阱；所以每个类比，我们都会标出它在哪里失效。
Analogy is a powerful tool for transfer, and also a trap; so we mark where it breaks down.
地图讲完了，但地图不等于地形。
The map is done. But a map is not the terrain.
开始之前，请带上三样东西。
Before we start, bring three things.
一点耐心：第二章的反向传播、第五章的注意力，是两个陡坡。
Patience: backpropagation in chapter two and attention in chapter five are the steep climbs.
一支笔：自测先写答案，再看解析；看懂不等于会做。
A pen: write your self-test answers before reading mine; understanding is not doing.
还有怀疑精神：找不到出处的说法，一律当作待验证。
And skepticism: any claim without a source counts as unverified.
下一章，我们把「猜下一个词」，写成一个可以计算的概率问题。
Next chapter, we turn guessing the next word into a computable probability problem.
顺便解释，为什么衡量猜得好不好，要用到「熵」。
Along the way, we'll see why judging how well it guesses calls for entropy.
第一章，语言的概率论。我们下期见。
Chapter one: the probability theory of language. See you next time.
